_comment: Fault catalogue used by the Fault Correlation Agent. primary = metrics that define the fault (min_primary_abnormal of them must be at least warning, default 1); supporting = symptoms it usually causes; contradicting = abnormal values that point to a different cause (contradict_upstream: also look on the path towards the internet). Pseudo-metrics: device_status (from infrastructure), telemetry_missing and downstream_impact (from connectivity). Add a new fault here without touching code.

link_congestion.label: Link congestion causing egress queue drops
actions: Inspect upstream and egress link utilisation on the affected device
Review QoS / queue configuration and traffic distribution
Identify top talkers; rate-limit or move bulk traffic off peak
Plan a capacity upgrade or add a parallel uplink (LACP) if utilisation stays above 80%

device_overload.label: Network device overloaded (CPU / memory exhaustion)
actions: Check the device process table for runaway processes (e.g. control-plane storms)
Look for broadcast storms or loops (spanning-tree events) driving CPU
Reduce control-plane load (logging, SNMP polling rate) and schedule a maintenance reload if memory leaks

hardware_failure.label: Hardware failure on the device (critical status, interface errors, CPU saturation)
actions: Fail traffic over to a redundant path or standby device if one exists
Check hardware logs, power supply, fans and temperature on the device
Reseat or replace the faulty line card / transceiver; open a hardware RMA if errors persist

interface_fault.label: Ethernet / interface fault (physical-layer errors on a link)
actions: Inspect and replace the patch cable / SFP transceiver on the affected port
Check duplex and speed negotiation on both ends of the link
Move the connection to a spare port to rule out a faulty switch port

weak_wifi_signal.label: Weak Wi-Fi signal causing retransmissions and poor performance
actions: Survey the zone; reposition the access point or add one to close the coverage gap
Check for co-channel interference and adjust channel / transmit power
Steer capable clients to 5 GHz and review minimum data-rate settings

dns_failure.label: DNS service failure (name resolution failing while the network path is healthy)
actions: Check the DNS server process and logs; restart the resolver if it is hung
Verify upstream forwarders are reachable and responding
Point clients to the secondary DNS server temporarily via DHCP option 6

dhcp_failure.label: DHCP service failure (clients cannot obtain IP addresses)
actions: Check DHCP server health and the address pool for the affected VLAN
Shorten lease time or extend the scope if the pool is exhausted
Verify the DHCP relay (ip helper-address) on the access-layer gateway

path_latency.label: Latency / jitter spike without local congestion (likely upstream or WAN path / routing issue)
actions: Trace the path (traceroute / MTR) from the affected segment to find the hop where latency rises
Check the upstream / ISP link and routing changes around the incident time
Escalate to the upstream provider if the delay is outside the campus network

upstream_device_outage.label: Upstream device outage affecting downstream devices
actions: Check power and reachability of the upstream device (console / out-of-band)
Verify the uplink between the upstream device and its parent
Fail downstream segments over to a redundant uplink if available
